Both sides traded blows in a match defined by tactical shifts and individual moments of brilliance. Early Disaster and Osasuna’s Surge The game began in the most unfortunate fashion for the hosts. Just three minutes into the match, Jeremy Toljan inadvertently sent the ball into his own net, gifting Osasuna an early lead. The visitors capitalized on this momentum quickly; in the 11th minute, Abel Bretones found Ante Budimir , who made no mistake with a clinical finish to double the advantage. It seemed as though Osasuna would run away with the game as Levante struggled to find their rhythm in the opening stages. The Victor Garcia Show Despite the two-goal deficit, Levante refused to capitulate. The tide began to turn in the 35th minute when Pablo Martinez set up Victor Garcia , who tapped the ball home to ignite the comeback. Barely two minutes later, Garcia struck again, this time firing a powerful right-footed shot from outside the box following an assist by Oriol Rey . Within a blink of an eye, the scores were level at 2-2, and the atmosphere reached a fever pitch. Red Card and Tactical Shifts Just before the halftime whistle, a pivotal moment occurred that changed the complexion of the match. Osasuna goalkeeper Sergio Herrera was shown a straight red card for handling the ball outside his area. This forced the visitors into an immediate change, with Aimar Oroz sacrificed to bring on substitute keeper Aitor Fernandez . The second half became a tactical battle, with Levante dominating possession while Osasuna retreated into a defensive shell. Late Drama in the Dying Minutes As the clock ticked toward full-time, the pressure from the home side became relentless. In the 90th minute, substitute Etta Eyong , who had been introduced to provide fresh attacking impetus, became the hero. Alan Matturro provided a pinpoint cross, and Eyong rose highest to head the ball home, sending the stadium into a frenzy. Despite a frantic five minutes of stoppage time, Levante held firm to secure a 3-2 victory, completing a remarkable turnaround in a classic football encounter.

Under the floodlights on May 2, 2026 , Barcelona traveled to face a resilient Osasuna side in a La Liga encounter that promised tactical intrigue. Both sides looked to impose their rhythm in a contest where every inch of turf was fiercely contested from the opening whistle. A Cagey Opening at El Sadar The first half was characterized by Barcelona ’s trademark territorial dominance, as the Catalan giants controlled 70% of the possession but struggled to find a clinical edge. Dani Olmo and Roony Bardghji were active in the early stages, frequently looking to exploit the flanks and delivering several corners, yet the Osasuna defense remained disciplined. The hosts were content to absorb pressure, leading to a string of goal kicks as the final ball from the visitors often lacked the necessary precision to trouble the goalkeeper. Despite the pressure from the visitors, it was Osasuna who came closest to breaking the deadlock in the 37th minute. Ante Budimir found himself with a golden opportunity to put the home side ahead, but his well-struck effort rattled against the post and stayed out. It was a massive let-off for Barcelona , who had dictated the tempo but lacked the bite to match their aesthetic buildup play. The half ended goalless, with Gavi picking up a yellow card as the physical nature of the contest began to ramp up. Tactical Adjustments and the Breakthrough The second half saw the intensity increase as both managers looked to their benches to find a solution. After Eric Garcia was cautioned for a tactical foul at the hour mark, Barcelona boss Hansi Flick opted for a triple substitution, introducing Marcus Rashford , Ferran Torres , and Frenkie de Jong . These changes injected immediate pace and directness into the Blaugrana attack, forcing Osasuna deeper into their own territory. The deadlock was finally broken in the 81st minute. Marcus Rashford , making an immediate impact, delivered a pinpoint cross into the heart of the box where Robert Lewandowski was waiting. The veteran striker rose highest to power a header home, finally giving Barcelona the lead they had craved. Just five minutes later, the visitors seemed to have put the game to bed. Fermin Lopez turned provider, finding Ferran Torres in space, and the Spanish international made no mistake with a sharp right-footed finish to make it 2-0. Late Drama and a Frantic Finish However, Osasuna refused to surrender. Just two minutes after Barcelona ’s second goal, the home side struck back to set up a grandstand finish. Substitute Abel Bretones swung in a dangerous cross that was met by Raul Garcia , whose header flew into the net to make it 2-1 in the 88th minute. The goal breathed new life into El Sadar, as the home fans rallied behind their team for one final push. The closing minutes were frantic and filled with missed opportunities at both ends. Ferran Torres had a chance to restore the two-goal cushion but uncharacteristically fired wide from a position he would usually convert. At the other end, Flavien Boyomo saw a header go agonizingly wide for the hosts during a period of sustained aerial bombardment. As tensions boiled over in the ninth minute of stoppage time, Enrique Barja was shown a yellow card for dissent, but the referee soon blew the final whistle to confirm a hard-fought victory for Barcelona .

The La Liga clash between Osasuna and Atletico Madrid on May 12, 2026 , proved to be a contest defined by tactical discipline and officiating drama. Both sets of supporters were treated to a high-intensity battle where every decision on the pitch carried significant weight. VAR Interventions and an Early Breakthrough The match began with high intensity as Osasuna tried to use their home advantage to unsettle the visitors. However, the momentum shifted early when a VAR review in the 12th minute led to a penalty for Atletico Madrid . Ademola Lookman stepped up to the spot and clinically converted with his right foot, sending Aitor Fernandez the wrong way to give the capital club the lead. Despite the setback, Osasuna pushed forward, with Ruben Garcia creating several chances from set-pieces, though they struggled to test Juan Musso effectively in the opening half-hour. High Tension and Overturned Decisions As the first half drew to a close, the game descended into a series of heated exchanges. Just before the break, it appeared Osasuna would have a golden opportunity to level the score when the referee initially awarded a penalty for a foul by Juan Musso on Ante Budimir . However, after another lengthy VAR check, the decision was revoked, much to the frustration of the home crowd and Budimir , who was cautioned for dissent shortly after. The atmosphere grew increasingly hostile as both teams struggled to maintain composure. Soerloth's Impact and a Numerical Disadvantage Diego Simeone introduced Alexander Soerloth at the start of the second half, and the Norwegian striker made an immediate impact. In the 71st minute, Marcos Llorente delivered a precise cross that Soerloth headed home from close range to double the lead. However, the match took another dramatic turn when Llorente , who had already been booked for dissent, received a second yellow card for a tactical foul in the 79th minute. This left Atletico Madrid to defend their lead with ten men for the final stages of the encounter. Late Drama in the Closing Minutes With a man advantage, Osasuna launched a relentless assault. Their persistence paid off in the 91st minute when Enrique Barja fired a left-footed strike into the net following an assist from Raul Garcia . The goal set up a frantic finish as Osasuna searched for an equalizer. Despite late pressure and several corners, Juan Musso stood firm, producing a series of saves to ensure Atletico Madrid escaped with all three points. The match concluded with a flurry of yellow cards as players from both sides, including Alejandro Catena and Robin Le Normand , were booked during a tense injury-time period.
